Question Description:
The State Meteorological Agency updates the National Climatological Data Bank daily, in which the climatological observations (precipitation and temperature) made in Spain for about 150 years are stored.

Nuria is studying the relationship between the variability of temperature and the hydric state of the soil in a dry region in Spain. To do this, they go to the Bank and request the temperature records in said area year after year since there are records.

In the first phase of his study, he tries to determine the number of peaks and valleys in temperatures in a given period of time. A temperature is considered peak (resp. Valley) in a sequence when the previous and the next in the sequence are strictly lower (resp. Higher).

Input Format:
The first line contains a number indicating the number of test cases listed below.

Each test case is made up of two lines. The first line has a single integer with the number of recorded temperatures (greater than 0 and less than or equal to 10,000), while the second line contains the sequence of temperatures (integers between −50 and 60 degrees Celsius).

Output Format:
Print the output in a separate lines contains, find the number of peaks and valleys will be written, separated by a space and followed by a line break.
